faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a commercial or multi-family EPDM roof in East Orange?

runs.v: Yes, once the work passes the threshold: a commercial, multi-family, or attached building requires a construction permit when roof work exceeds 25% of the total roof area in a 12-month period, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, and N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4 requires complete removal of a water-soaked covering or a roof already carrying 2 or more layers. Applications for East Orange New Jersey roofs go to the Building Division at the Department of Property Maintenance, East Orange City Hall, 44 City Hall Plaza.

faqs.q: How long does a commercial EPDM roof last on an East Orange apartment building?

runs.v: The average lifespan of an EPDM rubber roof is 15 to 25 years on the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, with a service-life study attributed via Progressive Materials citing 25 to 30 years and some industry sources 25 to 40 years with routine maintenance. Seam separation is the primary failure that shortens it.

faqs.q: Can my East Orange apartment building stay occupied during EPDM re-roofing?

runs.v: Yes. The work proceeds in phases, each section stripped and re-covered within a single shift so no dwelling unit sits exposed overnight, with access and staging coordinated with building management before work begins.

faqs.q: Does an EPDM roof on a historic East Orange building near Central Avenue need extra approval?

runs.v: East Orange has no identified local historic-preservation ordinance, so a Certificate of Appropriateness is not triggered, and a privately funded reroof on a Register-listed building is unrestricted, per the National Park Service. Verify current requirements with the city before work begins.

faqs.q: Why choose EPDM over TPO for an East Orange commercial roof?

runs.v: EPDM records 15 to 25 years on the InterNACHI chart against 7 to 20 years for TPO, and it typically installs for less, $7 to $10 per square foot against $8 to $12 for TPO; TPO's white surface reflects more summer heat. Both fail first at the seams.
